gdpPerCapita.note: GDP 52,669,500,000 2011 int$ (IMF via Economy of Yemen, rebased x 0.74) / population 41,773,878 (World Bank 2025) = 1,261. IMF quotes $1,657 per capita in current PPP on a different population base. Range +/-30%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x0.9365 because 98.1 is the 2012=100 vintage while ~132 is the 2017=100 vintage; same-vintage factor 91.478/132 = 0.693. Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. No SIPRI data since 2014 (3.97% then, World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS); war economy with external funding (Iran to the Houthis, Saudi Arabia/UAE to the PLC).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2018: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 25.4% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings. asOf 2018, very uncertain.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.05. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/YEM/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 31.62% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.21 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.19-0.23). Formula gives below 0 (1 - 0.316/0.21 = -0.51): farm employment exceeds calorie self-sufficiency, so farm households also eat imported wheat and part of a is qat, a non-food crop. Educated guess: mid 0.05 (0.02-0.10), the share of local grain, fruit, vegetables and fish that still reaches town markets. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 21% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports ~90% of staple food; famine conditions.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 21,165,097 x share of males aged 15-19 10.323% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 436,975. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

missiles.note: Educated guess. Houthi assembly of Iranian-designed missile kits; launchers produced locally (truck-mounted).

roadKm.note: Transport in Yemen article: 71,300 km of roads, 6,200 km paved (pre-war, undated). War damage not quantified (low).

railKm.note: Transport in Yemen article: there is no rail network.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 10 ports, 1 large + 2 medium = 3; key ports Aden, Al Hudaydah, Al Mukalla, Mocha, Ras Isa. Hudaydah damaged by Israeli/US strikes 2024-26 (low).

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Donkeys and camels widely used; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Yemen is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: high mountains, harsh terrain and climate, deep tribal support for the defender (Saudi-led intervention 2015-22 failed to dislodge the Houthis).

notes: DIVIDED-STATE WARTIME snapshot: Yemen has two rival authorities: the Houthi (Ansar Allah) Supreme Political Council holding Sanaa, the north-west and Hudaydah, and the internationally recognised Presidential Leadership Council seated in Aden with Saudi- and Emirati-backed forces; the STC was dissolved de jure on 9 Jan 2026 (STC article) and its forces absorbed into PLC structures. Forces here are the SUM of both sides on one ne:YEM polygon and overstate what either can field against an outsider. The Houthis are at war: Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab attacks (Sept 2026 crisis) and missile/drone waves on Saudi Arabia (Oct 2026). Capital is Sanaa (Houthi-held, de facto); the government sits in Aden. Almost every number is an educated guess (grade D) with wide ranges; GDP is the IMF estimate rebased (grade C). One-way attack drones excluded from drones per the role convention.
